A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OmniFlatten and provide readable main text, figures, tables, and Appendix A. The retained method and reorganized material can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: Section 4 and Tables 1–3 report original ASR, TTS, dialogue-quality, training-ablation, and turn-taking results.

after.justification: Section 4 and Tables 1–4 report original OmniFlatten results, including bilingual text and speech evaluations and results for the two-stream model.

M1.justification: Both versions retain Qwen2-0.5B, CosyVoice tokenization, the modality-alignment and four-/three-/two-stream training progression, and the same dialogue loss masking and chunking procedure. Revised explanations and additional evaluations do not establish an algorithmic or architectural change.

E1.justification: TTS evaluation switches from Librispeech/WenetSpeech to LibriTTS/AIShell-3, including replacing Mandarin meeting speech with a multi-speaker TTS corpus. The core English/Chinese ASR, TTS, and simulated voice-dialogue coverage remains.

E2.justification: V2 adds Whisper-small and reported VITA scores to ASR comparisons, retaining Whisper-Large-V3. TTS gains ChatTTS and CosyVoice comparators. Dialogue evaluation adds LLaMA-Omni, Moshi, GLM-Voice, and two Qwen2-Instruct sizes; turn-taking evaluation adds Moshi. V1's dialogue comparisons primarily involved internal ablations and ground-truth responses.

E3.justification: V2 changes English evaluation from CER to WER, uses Paraformer-zh for Chinese speech scoring, and adds WenetSpeech test-net. Chat evaluation explicitly focuses on single turns and adds ASR-transcribed speech scoring; turn-taking introduces a 1.5-second failure threshold. Reported dialogue sessions change from 360K to 390K and noise SNR from 15–25 to 15–30 dB.

E4.justification: V2 retains the modality-alignment and half-duplex-stage ablations, adds evaluation of the final two-stream model, and examines speech-versus-text outputs and comparisons with text-only models. The chunk-size-5 versus chunk-size-10 sensitivity analysis in v1 Table 3 is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. Both present point estimates; additional rows and changed numerical precision do not alter uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: The result tables are substantially replaced and expanded. V2 Table 3 newly reports two-stream speech scores of 2.19 for English and 3.06 for Chinese, below the corresponding three-stream scores of 3.92 and 5.15. Test-set CE losses disappear. Reported assistant/user response times change from 160/805 ms for v1's chunk-size-10 model to 193/287 ms, but revised data and evaluation rules prevent interpreting these as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The token-sequence specifications and verbal Acc@k definitions retain their mathematical substance. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions, proofs, or new derivations; the new response deadline is an experimental protocol rule.

C1.justification: The central claims about an unchanged GPT backbone, flattening, progressive training, and low-latency conversation remain. V2 promotes the already-described data-synthesis pipeline to an explicit contribution and removes the introduction's specific 160/805 ms results and strong assistant-versus-user turn-taking asymmetry claim.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations for speech-only degradation and speech/text performance gaps, plus limitations concerning model/data scale and conflicts between early stopping and alignment objectives. It also speculates that GLM-Voice's advantage reflects test-data leakage without demonstrating this. V1's detailed semantic-context and chunk-size explanations are removed; backchannel limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies the 15% high-quality WenetSpeech training subset, random user versus fixed assistant timbres, and Chinese ASR scoring resources. It removes the NanoGPT implementation pointer and the normal-distribution pause-sampling detail. These documentation changes do not establish corresponding changes to the underlying implementation.

R1.justification: V2 adds references and positioning around Mini-Omni2, GLM-4-Voice, LSLM, and dGSLM, plus the FunASR reference supporting Chinese recognition. The main contrasts with Moshi's parallel streams and SyncLM's deduplication remain.

P1.justification: The introduction is substantially condensed, related-work and evaluation narratives are rewritten, and method explanations are tightened. V2 adds a dedicated Limitations section and updates the author list and Appendix A heading. The appendix's evaluation prompt itself is unchanged.

P2.justification: V1 Figures 1–4 are consolidated into four panels of v2 Figure 1, and a new data-simulation diagram becomes Figure 2. The combined ASR/TTS table is split, dialogue tables gain language/modality groups and model sizes, and turn-taking rows change from chunk sizes to model comparisons.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses a central evidence gap: v1 evaluated three-stream textual responses while leaving the final speech-only model unscored. V2 adds external comparisons and ASR-transcribed speech evaluation, exposing two-stream weaknesses, and provides a Moshi turn-taking comparison and specific limitations. These substantially strengthen empirical assessment. Single-turn scoring narrows dialogue evaluation, the chunk-size analysis is lost, and the leakage attribution is unsupported, but these drawbacks do not outweigh the improved scrutiny of the proposed system.
